question: Should OpenClaw support an explicitly recorded expiry outcome for non-authorizing advisory plugin gates, while all execution-authorizing approvals remain fail-closed?
rationale: The current merged hardening intentionally removes runtime allow-on-timeout authority, while an active plugin use case requests a bounded advisory outcome; deciding whether that distinct capability belongs in the approval API requires product and security intent.

options.title: Separate advisory from execution approvals
options.body: Keep execution approvals deny-by-default and define any advisory expiry as a clearly non-authorizing, durable terminal outcome.

options.title: Keep one strict approval model
options.body: Retain fail-closed expiry for every approval request and direct soft workflow notifications to a separate mechanism.

options.title: Restore allow-on-timeout behavior
options.body: Permit request-level expiry allowance for plugin approvals, accepting a broader execution-authority compatibility and security contract.

recommendation.title: Separate advisory from execution approvals
recommendation.body: Keep execution approvals deny-by-default and define any advisory expiry as a clearly non-authorizing, durable terminal outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: The current main architecture and the linked merged approval series were authored through this coordinated implementation effort.
